item.title: Go Daily Question 20250605
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	var a = [5]int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
	var r [5]int

	for i, v := range a {
		if i == 0 {
			a[1] = 12
			a[2] = 13
		}
		r[i] = v
	}
	fmt.Println("r = ", r)
	fmt.Println("a = ", a)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
r =  [1 2 3 4 5]
a =  [1 12 13 4 5]

item.title: Go Daily Question 20250531
item.description:
What’s wrong with the following code?

func main() {
    fmt.Println([...]int{1} == [2]int{1})
    fmt.Println([]int{1} == []int{1})
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

There are two errors:

In Go, different types cannot be compared. The length of an array is part of its type, so [...]int{1} and [2]int{1} are two different types and cannot be compared. Slices cannot be compared.

item.title: Go Daily Question 214
item.description:
Below code output what?

func main() {
    a := [2]int{5, 6}
    b := [3]int{5, 6}
    if a == b {
        fmt.Println("equal")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("not equal")
    }
}
  • A. compilation error
  • B. equal
  • C. not equal
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Run online A. [2]int and [3]int are different types in Go and cannot be compared using the == operator.

./prog.go:8:10: invalid operation: a == b (mismatched types [2]int and [3]int)

item.title: Go Daily Question 186
item.description:
Differences between Arrays and Slices

🔑 Answer Analysis:
  1. Structural Comparison: A slice’s structure consists of three parts: length, capacity, and underlying array. An array’s structure is a contiguous block of memory.
  2. Functional Comparison: Slices are relatively flexible and support dynamic resizing based on capacity. The capacity of an array is fixed.
  3. Restriction Comparison: Arrays of the same type and capacity can be compared using the == operator, while slices cannot.

Frequently cited resource 🔗:Differences between Arrays and Slices

item.title: Go Daily Question 101
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {
    var a = [5]int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
    var r [5]int

    for i, v := range a {
        if i == 0 {
            a[1] = 12
            a[2] = 13
        }
        r[i] = v
    }
    fmt.Println("r = ", r)
    fmt.Println("a = ", a)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

r = [1 2 3 4 5] a = [1 12 13 4 5] The range expression participates in the loop with a copy, meaning that in the example, a copy of a is used in the loop, not the actual a.

item.title: Go Daily Question 046
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import (  
    "fmt"
)

func main() {  
    a := [5]int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
    t := a[3:4:4]
    fmt.Println(t[0])
}

A.3 B.4 C.compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B Analysis: t := a[3:4:4] A new slice t is generated based on slice a. The start of t points to the position of a[3], and stops at a[4].
